title: The soul enjoys scent (Berakhot 43b)
hookLine: a blessing over fragrance, the pleasure the soul enjoys, not the body
tomorrow: why would a man bless the road where a lion jumped him?

cards: A grandparent's coat in the closet still smells like them, years later, and one breath of it can undo a whole afternoon. Nobody gets full from that. Nothing is eaten.
So what does the soul enjoy that the body doesn't? The Talmud answers in one word: scent.

teach.b: The sages want a source for blessing a good smell, and they find it in the closing line of Psalm 150: "Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD."
The Hebrew word there for breath, neshamah, is also a word for soul. So they ask: what does the soul enjoy, and not the body? That's scent.
Food is shared by body and soul. A fragrance is the soul's alone, so it gets its own blessing.

teach.h: THE SPICE BOX, HAND TO HAND.
teach.b: You can hear it at the end of every Shabbat, when a family passes a box of spices hand to hand and blesses its smell. And notice how this week was built. Chanina ben Dosa kept praying with a snake at his heel.
Rabbi Chanina left one thing in our hands, awe. Moses prayed long, and short. A prayer flowed in the mouth.
The returners stood higher. And the earth changed hands with a blessing.
A whole week of the body teaching the soul: feet that didn't move, a mouth, a bowed head, a bite.
Today it's just a breath in.

how: Jews say blessings over pleasant smells, such as fragrant spices, herbs and trees, and at Havdalah, as Shabbat ends, a box of spices is passed around and blessed.

games.q: what does “the soul enjoys scent” mean?
o: fragrance is a pleasure for the soul alone, so it's blessed
incense was burned in the Temple to please God's nose
the soul leaves the body through the breath at death

games.q: this week, in pairs — tap them.
p: what the soul enjoys, not the body
kept praying with a snake at his heel

s: only food and drink get blessings in Jewish practice
a good smell gets its own blessing; the Talmud finds it in 'every thing that hath breath'.
the Talmud calls scent the pleasure the soul enjoys and the body doesn't
food is shared by body and soul; fragrance is the soul's alone.

games.q: a friend's grandmother has died. she gives you a scarf that still smells of her and says, "is it weird that i just smell it?" what does today's page offer her?
o: it's a little weird; better to keep a photo, since smells fade.
it's grief, and grief shouldn't get anything as holy as a blessing.
the sages call scent the soul's own pleasure, so it isn't weird at all.
games.why: on Berakhot 43b, scent is what the soul enjoys and the body doesn't. a breath of something beloved is exactly that kind of pleasure.

practice: Find something with a good smell: a spice from the kitchen, a cut orange, a flower, soap. Hold it close and breathe it in slowly, more than once.
If you know a blessing for fragrance, say it; if not, let the breath itself be the thanks.

wordCard.voice: The soul enjoys scent: the pleasure the body doesn't share, blessed because every thing that has breath praises.

orig.note: Hebrew: breath, and soul; 'every thing that hath breath' in Psalm 150.

carryVoice: From the spice box: the soul enjoys scent, even when nothing is eaten. A week of Berakhot, complete.

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 43b (the blessing over fragrance from Psalm 150:6; what the soul enjoys and not the body: scent)
